ticketComments.text:
Good Morning, I have received the following response from contentstack, let me know if we still need a demo from the team. Navigation inside Live Preview returns "Page Not Found" This is expected if the application's routing doesn't map 1:1 with the entry's url field. By default, Live Preview constructs the preview URL using the environment's Base URL and the entry's url field, which works for the root entry but may not work for custom or nested routes. For applications with a custom directory structure, the following are recommended: · Custom Preview URLs – Configure pattern-based preview URLs under Settings → Visual Experience → Preview URL . This supports placeholders such as /blog/{{entry.category}}/{{entry.slug}} , nested paths, taxonomy-driven URLs, and Base URL aliases for multiple hostnames. https://www.contentstack.com/docs/developers/set-up-live-preview/custom-preview-urls · Page Context – Call setPageContext() on each page to provide the current entryUid and contentTypeUid . This is the recommended approach when pages cannot be mapped directly from the entry's url field. This feature requires Live Preview Utils v4.4.4+ . https://www.contentstack.com/docs/developers/set-up-visual-builder/set-up-visual-builder-for-your-website Additionally, please verify that the website allows iframe embedding on all routes , not just the root page. If X-Frame-Options , Content-Security-Policy (frame-ancestors) , or a hard navigation redirects to a different host than the configured Base URL, the iframe will fail to load. https://www.contentstack.com/docs/content-managers/author-content/limitations-of-live-preview Live Preview button not working Please ask the customer to enable Display Setup Status under Settings → Live Preview . This runs the onboarding validation checks and reports the exact configuration issue instead of requiring manual troubleshooting. https://www.contentstack.com/docs/developers/set-up-live-preview/live-preview-onboarding-and-troubleshooting-guide Some common prerequisites to verify are: · Live Preview is enabled for the stack, a default preview environment is configured, and a Preview Token has been generated for the corresponding Delivery Token. https://www.contentstack.com/docs/developers/set-up-live-preview/set-up-live-preview-for-your-stack · The application is using the Preview Service rather than the legacy hash-only implementation. https://www.contentstack.com/docs/developers/set-up-live-preview/migrate-to-preview-service · stackSdk is passed to init() for CSR applications. Without it, preview hashes are not forwarded to Delivery SDK requests, resulting in published content (or no preview content). https://www.contentstack.com/docs/developers/set-up-live-preview/set-up-live-preview-for-your-website · SDK versions are compatible. Visual Builder requires: o Live Preview Utils v3.0+ o Delivery SDK v3.20.3+ o Live Preview Utils v4.4.4+ when using setPageContext() . Live Edit with addEditableTags() Relevant documentation: · Method reference, API signature, and the editButton object: https://www.contentstack.com/docs/developers/set-up-live-preview/set-up-live-edit-tags-for-entries-with-rest · Live Edit within Visual Builder: https://www.contentstack.com/docs/developers/set-up-visual-builder/set-up-visual-builder-for-your-website · Video walkthrough (~10 minutes): https://www.contentstack.com/academy/courses/implementing-live-preview/live-edit-tags For React applications, tagsAsObject should be set to true : addEditableTags(entry, contentTypeUid, true, locale); Then spread the generated attributes into JSX:

{data.name}

Using false generates a data-cslp string, which React cannot spread directly onto an element. ContentstackLivePreview.onEntryChange registers a callback that reads document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('[data-cslp]') and extracts attributes 'data-cslp-content-type-uid' and 'data-cslp-entry-uid'.

The onEntryChange callback creates a query via Stack.ContentType(contentTypeUid).Entry(entryUid).toJSON() and calls .fetch().
On successful fetch, the callback calls setPreviewPage([result]) where result is typed as IContentstackPage.
On fetch error, the callback calls .catch(() => {}) — errors are swallowed silently and prior previewPage state is preserved.
LivePreviewProvider state is: const [previewPage, setPreviewPage] = useState<[IContentstackPage] | undefined>(undefined).

LivePreviewContext is exported from src/context/contentstackContext.tsx with shape { previewPage?: [IContentstackPage]; setPreviewPage: Dispatch<SetStateAction<[IContentstackPage] | undefined>> } and default value { previewPage: undefined, setPreviewPage: () => undefined }.
useContent hook in src/hooks/useContent.ts reads both ContentstackContext and LivePreviewContext via useContext.
useContent computes effectiveContent = previewPage ? { ...content, page: previewPage } : content — when previewPage is defined, it overrides the page property of the existing content.
useContent returns { getContentByKey } where getContentByKey calls getValue<T>(effectiveContent, path, defaultValue).
When previewPage is undefined (no preview signal), effectiveContent equals the original content from ContentstackContext, so published content is rendered unchanged.
Homepage component in src/components/pages/Homepage.tsx receives props of type IHomepageProps { page: [IContentstackPage] } and does NOT directly call useContent — it reads page from props.
Homepage extracts pageComponents via getValue<PageComponents>(page, '0.modular_blocks', []) and recentNews via getValue<IRecentNews>(page, '0.recent_news', {}).

The onEntryChange callback supports multiple successive calls — each call fetches the entry and calls setPreviewPage with the new result, so successive draft changes update previewPage state in sequence.
There is no debounce, throttle, or deduplication logic in the onEntryChange callback — every entry change event triggers a new fetch and setPreviewPage call.
